description:
Bosnia and Herzegovina is facing growing political uncertainty after the surprise resignation announcement of the country’s High Representative — one of the most powerful international figures overseeing the post-war peace framework.

The High Representative plays a crucial role in implementing the Dayton Peace Agreement, with powers that can override local political decisions and carry the force of law.

Although the resignation was officially linked to personal reasons, many analysts see it as a symbolic victory for Bosnian Serb leader Milorad Dodik, who has long campaigned against the office and challenged its legitimacy.
Al Jazeera's Arduana Pribinja  reports from Sarajevo

description:
A new report alleges Israel secretly operated a covert military outpost deep inside the Iraqi desert during the recent conflict with Iran.

According to the report, the alleged base served as a logistical hub for Israeli air operations and included surveillance systems, helicopters, military vehicles, and advanced jamming equipment.

The operation was reportedly nearly exposed after a shepherd spotted helicopters in the area, prompting Iraqi security forces to investigate. Iraqi officials say troops later came under intense aerial fire, leaving one soldier dead and two others wounded.

Baghdad has since raised concerns over Iraqi sovereignty and submitted an official protest to the US-led coalition.

Iran has also reacted strongly to the allegations, warning that Israeli actions in the region continue to threaten regional stability.

Al Jazeera's Mahmoud Abdel-Wahed reports from the Iraqi capital.

author: Al Jazeera English
description:
The last oil tanker to leave the Middle East before the Iran war began has arrived in Long Beach, California, carrying 2 million barrels of oil. 
California has roughly six weeks of oil and gas left, with the state importing about a third of its foreign oil from the Gulf. The Strait of Hormuz remains effectively closed, and gas prices in California have jumped to nearly $6 a gallon, with some stations charging $8. 
Nationwide, gas prices have risen from 2.90to4.45 per gallon since the war began. Diesel prices have spiked 48 percent, truckers are avoiding long-haul loads, farmers face fertilizer shortages as ships sit idle, and fishermen are struggling to cover fuel costs.
So, can California avoid running out of energy? And will the rest of the US feel the pain as the Strait of Hormuz remains shut?

Presenter: Cyril Venier

Guests:
Stan Veuger, Senior Fellow in Economic Policy Studies at the American Enterprise Institute

In the first round of evacuations from the Canary Islands, 94 people from 16 nationalities were repatriated, though some may carry the rare respiratory virus spread through contact with rat droppings. 
The World Health Organisation recommends a 42-day quarantine for anyone exposed, but quarantine protocols vary by country, ranging from 45 days in Greece to just 72 hours in the UK. 
Despite precautions, specialists stress the risk of wider transmission is extremely low, unlike COVID-19, and authorities say the outbreak is under control.

description:
It's been four years since Israeli forces shot and killed veteran Al Jazeera journalist Shireen Abu Akleh
The veteran Palestinian-American correspondent was covering an Israeli raid in Jenin refugee camp, while wearing a clearly marked press vest, standing among several other journalists.
That's when an Israeli soldier shot her in the neck and killed her. She was 51.

Palestinian journalist Ali al-Samoudi was near Shireen when she was killed. 
He was also injured during the Israeli attack.
A year ago, Israeli authorities arrested the 59-year-old and held him without charge or trial.
He was one of more than a hundred Palestinian journalists who have been detained and imprisoned since October the 7th, 2023.
He was recently released and he returned with significant weight loss.
Despite everything, Ali al-Samoudi is still committed to sharing Shireen's story.

Al Jazeera’s Nida Ibrahim reports from Jenin, occupied West Bank.

description:
The International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) field hospital in Rafah is one of very few functional health facilities in the south of Gaza, serving as a primary healthcare provider in the area. 
Recently, it saw the entry of medical equipment crucial to respond to the medical needs of people in Gaza, but the organization warns that a single field hospital cannot cope with the "sheer scale" of what is needed.  

Healthcare in Gaza has become “a casualty of the armed conflict”, says Pat Griffiths, a spokesperson for the ICRC in Rafah, adding that hospitals in the besieged enclave “don’t look like how a hospital should, riddled with bullets, or damaged by explosive blasts”.
